heading: Bio
paragraphs: Daisy Nduta is a Kenyan female audio engineer & sound recordist, an award-winning multidisciplinary creative and cultural producer with around a decade of experience working across sound, events, film, artist development and community-led arts. Her practice sits where technical craft meets collaboration, shaped by years of working between Kenya and Australia.

Daisy trained as a sound engineer at SAE Institute, Melbourne. While still a student, she started Wazi, a self-produced podcast that led to her being invited to the Emerging Writers’ Festival as a sound artist. Producing her final project, Kaya, became her first show and her entry into event production, and led to the opportunity to present Assimilate at Melbourne Fringe Festival (2019), where it won a Young Creatives Award. That success brought opportunities to produce and curate shows for Melbourne Music Week and MPavilion.

After university, Daisy worked for companies setting up concerts and festivals, building her live production experience, while also building her film portfolio through sound recording and sound design on her peers’ films, including Blackwood. She then joined the community radio station Triple R (RRR) as a podcast editor, became an assistant broadcast engineer for live-to-air shows, then a fill-in host, and went on to present her own show, So Fresh So Clean. She was also commissioned as a consultant on the Future Reset Project: Diasporic Dreaming, helping design programs for young people from African Diaspora communities.

Since returning to Kenya, Daisy has worked across the full range of her practice. She coordinated Frequency Shift, a community-driven multimedia project at The Mall in Westlands, Nairobi, supported by Africa - Europe Spaces of Culture (EUNIC), which connected radio, podcasting and immersive media across four organisations. She has also produced and curated showcases at Kilele Summit. As a location sound recordist and sound designer, she has joined crews on films and documentaries, including Mwakenya (NBO Film Festival), and worked on sound design for clients such as HBS. Through artist development, she managed mau from nowhere, leading creative direction, strategy and partnerships.
Currently based in Nairobi, working across Africa and beyond.
